definitions.prime_shell: V_p=T^2[p] minus {0}, identified with F_p^2 minus {0}; every point has exact additive order p
definitions.primitive_orbits: Gamma_p is the set of least-period A-orbits partitioning V_p
definitions.orbit_length: |gamma| is the least dynamical period of gamma
definitions.unramified_period: tau_p is the order of A in GL_2(F_p) for p not equal to 5
definitions.point_observable: L(x)=log(ord(x)); on V_p it is the constant log(p)
definitions.raw_return_product: the fixed-point exponential using Birkhoff sums S_n L
definitions.orbit_label_product: the distinct formal product assigning log(p) once per primitive orbit independent of |gamma|
definitions.local_variable: z=p^(-s) for a fixed shell p

frozen_theorem_claims: T1: p=2 gives one orbit of length 3 and m_2=1.

T2: for odd split p not equal to 5, tau_p divides p-1, every nonzero point has exact period tau_p, and m_p=(p+1)*h_p with h_p=(p-1)/tau_p; the eigenlines give 2*h_p cycles and the complement gives (p-1)*h_p cycles.
T3: for odd inert p, tau_p divides p+1, every nonzero point has exact period tau_p, and m_p=(p-1)*h_p with h_p=(p+1)/tau_p.
T4: at p=5, four points have exact period 2 and twenty points have exact period 10, giving two cycles of each length and m_5=4.
T5: p=2 is the unique prime with m_p=1, and every odd prime satisfies m_p at least p-1.
T6: the raw-return factor is the product over gamma of (1-p^(-s*|gamma|))^(-1); p=5 has separate length-2 and length-10 factors.
T7: the unweighted orbit-label factor is (1-p^(-s))^(-m_p), with logarithmic repeat coefficient m_p/r.
T8: for every odd p, no pure scalar denominator product with fixed nonzero coefficients w_gamma independent of z equals (1-z)^(-1); if zeros are allowed, equality requires the multiset {1,0,...,0}.
T9: the fractional shell product with outer exponent |gamma|/(p^2-1) equals one Euler factor, but is global normalized counting and extends mechanically to composite exact-order shells.
T10: the global label logarithm diverges for real 1<s<=2, is not absolutely convergent for complex 1<Re(s)<=2, and is absolutely convergent for Re(s)>3; no exact abscissa is claimed.

odd_inert.normal_form: multiplication by lambda in F_(p^2), with lambda^p=lambda^(-1)

point_potential_raw_return.definition: exp(sum_(n>=1) (1/n) sum_(x in V_p intersect Fix(A^n)) exp(-s*S_n L(x)))
point_potential_raw_return.repeat_ledger: an orbit of length ell contributes p^(-s*r*ell)/r at traversal r
point_potential_raw_return.semantic_warning: Birkhoff accumulation preserves dynamical return length

orbit_label.semantic_warning: log(p) is assigned once per orbit by a global shell label, not by the raw point-potential return law

product_semantics_lock.period_normalization_boundary: dividing a raw orbit sum by its primitive period repairs the label length but retains all m_p orbit factors

scalar_weight_obstruction.coefficient_domain: fixed scalar coefficients independent of z
scalar_weight_obstruction.nonzero_assumption: w_gamma is nonzero for every gamma
scalar_weight_obstruction.finite_scalar_or_holder_scope: w_gamma=exp(S_gamma phi) is nonzero for a finite scalar or Holder potential and is covered only when used in the frozen pure denominator form
scalar_weight_obstruction.proof: nonzero leading coefficient gives denominator degree m_p; degree one requires m_p=1
scalar_weight_obstruction.zero_weight_boundary: equality with zeros requires exactly one weight equal to 1 and all remaining weights equal to 0
scalar_weight_obstruction.equal_weight_control: w_gamma=1/m_p gives sum_gamma w_gamma^r=m_p^(1-r), so only r=1 is repaired when m_p>1

composite_extension.exact_order_shell: E_q={x in T^2: additive order exactly q}
composite_extension.cardinality: J_2(q)=q^2*product over primes ell dividing q of (1-ell^(-2))
composite_extension.conclusion: mechanical for every finite permutation of an exact-order shell and therefore not prime-specific

one_orbit_selector.effect: one retained orbit produces one factor
one_orbit_selector.cost: discard m_p-1 orbits and add a global shell selector

centralizer_escape_boundary.inert_shell: centralizer F_(p^2)^x acts transitively on the nonzero shell
centralizer_escape_boundary.split_shell: diagonal centralizer has the two nonzero eigenlines and their complement as three natural strata
centralizer_escape_boundary.ramified_shell: Jordan kernel minus zero and its complement form two natural strata
centralizer_escape_boundary.paper9_claim: no quotient or canonical selector is constructed or ruled out
centralizer_escape_boundary.label_provenance_warning: a p-shell quotient still depends on the shell centralizer and receives its prime label from the externally specified additive-order shell

stop_rules: No Paper-9 code authoring or execution is authorized by this source lock.
No registered audit may run before a fresh independent deployment pass bound to the final source-lock and future code-tree hashes.
Any source hash, upstream hash, matrix, field size, period, cycle count, factor, rational coefficient, or proof-contract disagreement stops the audit.
No new prime, composite order, matrix, potential, normalization, selector, repetition range, or analytic evaluation point may be added after lock.
No external prime table, generated prime target array, Riemann-zero data, numerical s grid, numerical logarithm, optimizer, tolerance match, or network access is permitted during execution.
The five-prime reproduction is development-seen and may not be called blind or promoted to all-prime or convergence evidence.
A passing audit does not change the low-novelty verdict and cannot open Route B.
Centralizer quotient work is reserved for Paper 10 and may not be investigated or declared impossible in Paper 9.
The scalar denominator theorem may not be extended to matrix-valued, numerator-bearing, alternating, Fredholm, transfer, or cohomological products.
No exact abscissa, conditional convergence, analytic continuation, Riemann-zero, transfer, quantization, or historical-priority claim may be inferred.

mandatory_nonclaims: The prime-lattice orbit classification and finite-lattice Euler-product framework are classical, not new Paper-9 results.
The raw point-potential return product and the orbit-label product are distinct and neither may be silently substituted for the other.
The scalar no-go is only a pure denominator polynomial-degree statement for fixed nonzero scalar coefficients independent of the local variable.
Matrix-valued factors, numerator or alternating cancellation, transfer/Fredholm determinants, and cohomological superdeterminants are not excluded.
Fractional shell normalization succeeds exactly; it is rejected only as global, tautological, and non-prime-specific.
One-orbit selection succeeds after symmetry breaking and discarding other orbits; no universal selector impossibility is claimed.
A centralizer quotient is a real outside-theorem escape reserved for Paper 10.
No claim is made for 2<Re(s)<=3, an exact abscissa, conditional convergence, analytic continuation, or zeros.
The fixed five-prime audit cannot prove the all-prime theorem or any analytic statement.
No prime-orbit bijection, canonical selector, prime-generating mechanism, transfer theorem, prime/zero correspondence, quantization, historical priority, or Route B is claimed.
